fields.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO.
fields.note: Core elements are supported: options 1-3, occupant protections, penalties, highest-amount rule, and the 15-day RSO/JCO payment. The document says the 15-day payment applies to all tenants. The phrase 'All tenants get at least the RSO or JCO amounts' is a fair paraphrase of 'minimum of the RSO or JCO amounts'.

Chart B values match for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 (Extremely Low, Very Low, Low). The document states that above-low-income households are paid under Chart A. The $250,000 per displaced unit penalty and the 5-year window are also stated. The 5-year window runs from the filing, so 'look-forward from filing' is acceptable.
The document also says the City Council adopted the RPO on February 11, 2025.
The bulletin is current (Rev 07.01.2026) and describes the RPO as operative, so in_force is consistent.

fields.quoted_span:
The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the 
purpose of new construction.
fields.note: The Protected Unit definition (covenant, rent control, lower/very low income rental within 5 years, Ellis Act withdrawal within 10 years) and 'All RSO units are Protected Units' are in the document. The regular RSO/JCO rules apply if units are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant. Enhanced relocation is limited to lower-income (80% AMI) tenants.
Ordinances 188481 and 188482 are cited in the document, and the 'Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO)' name is also used.
